canonical_answers: Doubling the path difference to 2.50 m gives Δ/λ = 5.0 (integer), so the interference shifts from destructive to constructive.

payload.text: Two coherent sources have wavelength 0.500 m and path difference 1.25 m at a detector.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Predict how the observable changes when the defining scale parameter is doubled, and justify the prediction quantitatively.

criteria.description: Doubling the path difference from 1.25 m to 2.50 m changes the ratio Δ/λ from 2.5 (a half-integer number of wavelengths, destructive interference) to 5.0 (an integer number of wavelengths, constructive interference); the detector shifts from destructive to constructive interference.
required_evidence: ratio Δ/λ = 5.0, an integer number of wavelengths
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show doubled path difference = 2.50 m; ratio Δ/λ = 5.0, an integer number of wavelengths; prediction: constructive interference (shift from destructive).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the number of wavelengths contained in the path difference determines interference type, and how the coherent-source assumption is required for this ratio to determine interference type consistently.
